destination.title: Axion geometry, interactions and cosmological control
destination.question: How do axion geometry, potential generation and interactions enable or limit controlled effective theories and cosmological evolution, and which conclusions depend on specified quantum-gravity assumptions?
destination.summary: The original numerical membership establishes neither a common mechanism nor a universal constraint. A useful parent connects range engineering, compactification control, potential generation, conditional consistency criteria and distinct cosmological applications. Public directions reuse existing questions across numerical batches; batch scopes remain provenance.

sources.title: Axion decay constants away from the lamppost

evidence.text: How large can axion periods become in controlled string compactifications, including small-radius regions, and which geometric or duality effects limit their growth? The paper seeks quantitative examples rather than a general quantum-gravity bound.

sources.title: Swampland distance conjecture, inflation and $\alpha$-attractors

evidence.text: How does axionic motion change the proper excursion associated with a fixed radial approach to infinite distance?

sources.title: Completing natural inflation

evidence.text: Can natural inflation obtain a sufficiently flat axion potential and an effectively super-Planckian axion scale while keeping the underlying axion scales sub-Planckian?

sources.title: N-vaton

evidence.text: How do many light curvatons with simultaneous decay generate primordial power and local non-Gaussianity, what conditionally bounds fNL, and can KKLT axions realize this scenario?

sources.title: Searching for axions and ALPs from string theory

evidence.text: Which closed-string axions survive moduli stabilization in type IIB flux compactifications, what masses and visible-sector couplings does the LARGE Volume Scenario predict, and which searches could probe them?

sources.title: A review of Axion Inflation in the era of Planck

evidence.text: How can axion shift symmetry protect inflation from ultraviolet corrections, which constructions realize sufficient inflation, and what signatures and constraints follow in the Planck-2013 observational setting?

sources.title: N-flation with Hierarchically Light Axions in String Compactifications

evidence.text: Can perturbative LVS stabilisation produce many axions hierarchically lighter than their geometric partners, allowing collective inflation or quintessence with sub-Planckian individual decay constants?

sources.title: F-term Axion Monodromy Inflation

evidence.text: Can perturbative F-term potentials realize axion monodromy with super-Planckian excursions, an underlying supersymmetric description, and protection against the supergravity eta problem?

sources.title: Towards Universal Axion Inflation and Reheating in String Theory

evidence.text: Can the universal axion support natural or flux-induced monodromy inflation in a type IIB large-volume framework, while remaining lighter than stabilized saxions and preferentially reheating Standard Model particles?

sources.title: Aligned Natural Inflation: Monodromies of two Axions

evidence.text: Can alignment of two axions provide the large effective displacement needed for natural inflation while keeping individual decay constants below the Planck scale, and how does the misalignment parameter determine the predicted scalar and tensor spectra?

sources.title: Combining Universal and Odd RR Axions for Aligned Natural Inflation

evidence.text: Can KNP alignment of the universal RR axion C0 and one orientifold-odd C2 axion produce a trans-Planckian effective decay constant in weakly coupled type IIB large-volume compactifications while retaining moduli stabilization?

sources.title: Trajectories with suppressed tensor-to-scalar ratio in Aligned Natural Inflation

evidence.text: Which inflationary trajectories occur in the general two-axion aligned potential, and can their scalar tilt, tensor amplitude or gauge-field couplings distinguish Aligned Natural Inflation from single-field Natural Inflation?

sources.title: Diluting the inflationary axion fluctuation by a stronger QCD in the early Universe

evidence.text: Can supersymmetric axion models accommodate high-scale primordial inflation, sufficiently small axion isocurvature, and axions constituting all dark matter through an early period of stronger QCD?

sources.title: On Natural Inflation and Moduli Stabilisation in String Theory

evidence.text: Can flux-induced axion alignment produce a controlled super-Planckian effective decay constant once the same fluxes' effects on moduli and instanton amplitudes are included?

sources.title: Relaxion Monodromy and the Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Can cosmological relaxation preserve the axion's discrete gauge identification during enormous field excursions, and can membrane transitions required by a suitable Weak Gravity Conjecture leave the scanning dynamics under control?

sources.title: Subleading Effects and the Field Range in Axion Inflation

evidence.text: Can significant but subleading nonperturbative axion corrections enhance inflationary e-folds, reduce the required field range and decay constant, and produce distinctive observables instead of trapping the inflaton or merely perturbing smooth slow roll?

sources.title: Backreacted Axion Field Ranges in String Theory

evidence.text: Can closed-string axions acquire parametrically super-Planckian proper excursions through flux-induced monodromy or alignment once the same fluxes and axion energy backreact on their field-space metric?

sources.title: Backreaction Issues in Axion Monodromy and Minkowski 4-forms

evidence.text: Why does a Kaloper–Sorbo coupling fail to guarantee a transplanckian axion range in string compactifications, and is the onset of saxion backreaction necessarily tied to the Planck scale?

sources.title: Axion Inflation and Affleck-Dine Baryogenesis

evidence.text: Can axion-dependent higher-dimensional couplings drive Affleck–Dine baryogenesis after axion inflation when the Hubble-induced and soft A-term phases coincide, or even when the soft A-term is absent?

sources.title: Backreaction in Axion Monodromy, 4-forms and the Swampland

evidence.text: Can an axion wind over a transplanckian proper distance while other compactification fields remain stabilized and below the effective-theory cutoff? The relevant range is determined by the backreacted metric, rather than coordinate displacement alone.

sources.title: Systematics of Aligned Axions

evidence.text: How can exact and approximate shift symmetries make multi-axion potentials tractable, allowing systematic characterization of critical points, vacuum energies and smooth field-space regions relevant to inflation?

sources.title: Large Field Inflation/Quintessence and the Refined Swampland Distance Conjecture

evidence.text: Can an axion traverse a large canonical distance in a string-derived cosmological effective theory while heavy fields remain stabilized and all retained masses remain below the ultraviolet cutoff?

sources.title: Large Field Inflation/Quintessence and the Refined Swampland Distance Conjecture

evidence.text: Which compactification fields can remain light without disrupting late cosmology? The review distinguishes shift-protected axions from gravitationally decaying scalar moduli that can spoil nucleosynthesis.

sources.title: Mass Hierarchies and Dynamical Field Range

evidence.text: The closed-string example asks whether a previously reported flux-independent critical axion range survives the kinetic self-consistency test when the axion cannot be parametrically separated from the other moduli.

sources.title: Mass Hierarchies and Dynamical Field Range

evidence.text: The model tests whether a light open-string axion can move while stabilized closed-string moduli contribute negligibly to the field-space length. Its independent superpotential coefficient mu permits a formal heavy-to-light hierarchy.

sources.title: Mass Hierarchies and Dynamical Field Range

evidence.text: When does a distance computed by displacing one axion and readjusting potential minima describe the field distance actually traversed? The distinction matters because a failure of this approximation does not by itself establish the breakdown of the underlying multifield effective theory.

sources.title: Phases of Inflation

evidence.text: How do instantons, confinement and four-fermion interactions generate masses and inflationary potentials in string-inspired axion–chiral gauge theories, and which phases admit single-field inflation?

sources.title: De Sitter vs Quintessence in String Theory

evidence.text: Can many light axions make hilltop initial conditions plausible? The authors appeal to inflationary displacement and an approximately uniform spread over one period without deriving a probability for successful quintessence.

sources.title: Cosmological window onto the string axiverse and the supersymmetry breaking scale

evidence.text: Can cosmological constraints inform the string-instanton action S and supersymmetry-breaking scale Msusy, and how strongly do the inferred axion properties depend on string-inspired versus phenomenological priors?

sources.title: Virtual and Thermal Schwinger Processes

evidence.text: How does electric flux dissipate when its direction is a small spatial circle, how does this differ from thermal pair creation, and can the resulting axion fragmentation constrain homogeneous field excursions?

sources.title: N-vaton

evidence.text: Applies the stated Cauchy–Schwarz inequality to power-normalized curvaton weights and mass-weighted field sums to obtain conditional lower and upper bounds.

sources.title: Searching for axions and ALPs from string theory

evidence.text: The review organizes axion spectra by the corrections used to stabilize Kähler moduli: nonperturbative superpotentials, perturbative and nonperturbative Kähler-potential corrections, and D-terms. It then relates the surviving spectra to dark-matter production and photon-conversion searches.

sources.title: A review of Axion Inflation in the era of Planck

evidence.text: For Abelian production, the review presents helicity mode equations, constant-ξ Coulomb-function solutions and an adiabatic-vacuum approximation. Backreaction is described through a mean-field inflaton equation and an approximate sourced perturbation equation.

sources.title: N-flation with Hierarchically Light Axions in String Compactifications

evidence.text: Expands the N=1 F-term potential in inverse volume, combining α′ corrections, small-cycle nonperturbative effects, string loops and large-cycle nonperturbative terms. Extended no-scale cancellation makes the loop potential subleading despite its larger correction to the Kähler potential.

sources.title: F-term Axion Monodromy Inflation

evidence.text: D-brane DBI reduction determines field-dependent kinetic terms and potentials; canonical normalization changes their asymptotic powers. T-duality relates massive Wilson lines to brane positions in flux backgrounds.

sources.title: Towards Universal Axion Inflation and Reheating in String Theory

evidence.text: Reheating estimates use axion–gauge couplings on magnetized D7-branes, axion mixing, and the quoted dimension-five decay formula Γ=g²mθ³/(64πMpl²). D7- and D3-tadpole constraints determine the assumed available sectors.

sources.title: Large field inflation from D-branes

evidence.text: Can D-brane-generated F-term axion monodromy provide large-field inflation with an inflaton lighter than stabilized moduli, controlled stabilizer dynamics and a flattened potential at trans-Planckian field values?

sources.title: Instanton Interactions and the Axion Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Can the axionic Weak Gravity Conjecture be formulated sharply through nonbinding long-distance interactions of identical instantons, and under which scalar-field assumptions does that condition imply a bound on the axion decay constant and instanton action?

When does a nonperturbatively generated equilibrium effective potential describe real-time axion dynamics, and how can corrections from the integrated-out sector be incorporated?

The local setting isolates the instability of an axion placed close to the maximum of a periodic potential. Negative potential curvature competes with Hubble damping and determines how rapidly the field leaves its initial position.

An axion initially near a potential maximum can remain potential dominated before its tachyonic displacement grows. The question is whether a single cosine reliably estimates that interval when the potential receives higher harmonics or light-meson mixing.
Can natural inflation obtain a sufficiently flat axion potential and an effectively super-Planckian axion scale while keeping the underlying axion scales sub-Planckian?

Can string/M-theory periodic fields have parametrically super-Planckian decay constants that provide sufficiently slow potential variation for natural inflation, or the much larger field ranges contemplated in anthropic cosmological-constant scenarios?

destination.title: Primordial features across CMB, matter and induced waves
destination.question: How do specified inflationary mechanisms generate spectral features, and under what scale, transfer and measurement assumptions can CMB, matter or scalar-induced gravitational-wave observations retain and distinguish those features?
destination.summary: A shared target connecting feature generation, observational transfer and recovery across probes. The mechanisms, scales and forecast conditions remain distinct.

systems: Inflationary models with specified spectral-feature mechanisms
Two-field models producing sharp, resonant or combined standard-clock features
targets: Generation of oscillatory or scale-dependent primordial spectra
Survival of spectral information through transfer
assumptions: Features accessible to different probes need not arise at the same scale or from the same model.
The supplied two-field examples require tuning of feature location and amplitude.

sources.title: Running Spectral Index from Inflation with Modulations

evidence.text: Can repeated small modulations of an inflaton potential generate a sizable negative running across CMB scales while retaining prolonged slow-roll inflation, and what subsequent small-scale spectrum would distinguish this mechanism?

sources.title: Resonant features in the stochastic gravitational wave background

evidence.text: How do resonant, log(k)-periodic features in an enhanced primordial scalar power spectrum appear in the post-inflationary scalar-induced gravitational wave background, and what scalar-spectrum information could their modulations reveal?

sources.title: Detecting primordial features with LISA

evidence.text: Can LISA reconstruct oscillatory features in scalar-induced stochastic gravitational waves, and which signal parameters permit accurate measurements? The study distinguishes sharp versus resonant features and inflationary versus post-inflationary production.

sources.title: Running Spectral Index from Inflation with Modulations

evidence.text: Numerically solve the inflaton equation and Friedmann equation, then evaluate Pζ≈H⁴/(4π²φ̇²) at horizon exit. This supplies numerical background evolution with the stated approximate perturbation prescription.

sources.title: Resonant features in the stochastic gravitational wave background

evidence.text: Insert the modulated scalar spectrum into the quadratic GW integral and separate terms of order Alog⁰, Alog¹ and Alog². Logarithm identities and trigonometric product identities factor out the k dependence; the remaining kernel integrals determine frequency-dependent amplitudes and phases.

sources.title: Detecting primordial features with LISA

evidence.text: Mock observations assume four years with 75% efficiency, split into approximately 11.5-day segments, giving approximately 10^-6 Hz resolution. Gaussian signal and noise realizations are self-correlated, averaged and coarse-grained. PCA examples use the single TDI X stream.

sources.title: Running Spectral Index from Inflation with Modulations

evidence.text: Compare the modulated spectrum with a constant-running extrapolation Pζ(k)=Pζ(k0)(k/k0)^{ns(k0)−1+(α/2)ln(k/k0)}, normalized to the same pivot observables.

sources.title: Running Spectral Index from Inflation with Modulations

evidence.text: Expand slow-roll estimates for ns−1≈−6ε+2η and dns/dlnk≈−24ε²+16εη−2ξ, retaining the smooth contribution and leading oscillatory corrections under a hierarchy of modulation derivatives.

sources.title: Resonant features in the stochastic gravitational wave background

evidence.text: A complementary peak-comb analysis applies the imported resonance-location rule kmax,ij=(k*i+k*j)/√3, subject to kmax,ij>|k*i−k*j|. The authors compare its predictions and their semi-analytic templates with numerical spectra.

sources.title: Probing Primordial Features with the Stochastic Gravitational Wave Background

evidence.text: Can amplified primordial features produce a scalar-induced stochastic gravitational wave background detectable by space interferometers, especially LISA, while retaining spectral information about inflationary dynamics? Can reconstruction or analytical templates distinguish the resulting feature classes?

sources.title: Natural inflation, Planck scale physics and oscillating primordial spectrum

evidence.text: Can Planck-scale corrections to a natural-inflation potential generate oscillating or scale-dependent primordial spectra, and could their signatures survive transfer into CMB temperature, polarization, and matter spectra?
